digest.key_takeaway: AWS has released Amazon ECS Gateway, an account-level ingress resource letting platform teams define networking once and application teams opt services in with a connector. Each service gets a generated hostname and routing is host-based, and neither the announcement nor the documentation covers custom domains. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: Hydrogen-1.0: open-weight scientific model beats GPT-6 Astra on FSR with 72% lower estimated output cost [P]
articles.summary: Hey everyone— we’re the Deep Principle team behind Mira AI Scientist. We just released Hydrogen-1.0, an open-weight model post-trained from GLM-5.3 for chemistry, materials science, and life sciences. Here’s how it performed in our evaluations:  FrontierScience Research: 38.3% pass rate vs. 33.3% for GPT-6 Astra at max thinking—a 5 percentage point lead. Estimated output-side cost on FSR: $0.25 per problem vs. $0.88 for Astra at max thinking—about 72% lowerunder our evaluation setup. GPQA Diamond: 92.9% accuracy, compared with Kimi K3’s 93.5%. articles.title: AI governance that fits in a pull request
articles.summary:
Most AI governance lands on engineering teams as a document. Someone writes an acceptable use policy, it is circulated, and nothing about how anyone works actually changes. Six months later a customer asks which of their data has been sent to a model provider and the policy turns out not to answer that.

Governance only holds when it is a property of the workflow rather than a file in the wiki. Below is what that looks like in practice for a team that ships software, with the controls expressed as things that happen in a repository rather than things people are supposed to remember.

articles.title: CPU parallelism lessons that carry over to GPU kernels: dependency chains, FP non-associativity, false sharing, memory-bound loops [P]
articles.summary: Session 2 of my free GPU kernel engineering series (my own channel, earlier post: [LINK TO FIRST POST]) covers CPU parallelism, with no GPU code. The idea is that most GPU performance ideas are CPU ideas turned up, so here are the parts I found most useful on their own.  A single accumulator is a dependency chain. In `sum += a[i] * b[i]` every add waits on the previous one, so the loop uses a fraction of the core.
